title: Portfolio Extra: Library Management System
descriptionMarkdown:
# Library Management System

## Position in the curriculum
Build this once you have completed Chapters 6 through 11 (enums/records/sealed types, inheritance and interfaces, generics, collections, algorithms, and exceptions). It is an optional, differently-domained companion to Phase 2's issue tracker, not a replacement for it: this project's focus is modeling physical/borrowable inventory and its lifecycle, not priority ordering or dependency graphs.

## Already-proven foundation
Chapter 10's phase checkpoint already proved you can build a correctly ordered, duplicate-rejecting index over records. This project reuses that same discipline — correct equality, correct ordering, correct rejection of invalid input — applied to a library's catalog and its borrowers instead of an issue list.

## Project scope
Model `Book` (ISBN, title, author, copy count) and `Member` as records or well-encapsulated classes; use a sealed interface for loan outcomes (`Approved`, `Denied(reason)`, `AlreadyReturned`) rather than a boolean or a magic string. A `LibraryCatalog` owns the invariant that a book cannot be checked out more times than it has physical copies, and that returning a copy never already returned is rejected without corrupting the count. Support: add/remove a book title, check out a copy to a member (respecting a configurable per-member loan limit), return a copy, search by title/author (case-insensitive, partial match), and list overdue loans given an injected clock. Throw specific, named exceptions (`NoCopiesAvailableException`, `MemberLoanLimitExceededException`, `BookNotFoundException`) rather than a generic `RuntimeException`, and preserve catalog state on every rejected operation.

## Required evidence
- Equality/hashCode tests for `Book` keyed by ISBN, including two books with identical titles but different ISBNs.
- A boundary table and tests for checkout at exactly the last available copy, checkout when none remain, and return without a matching outstanding loan.
- A custom exception hierarchy with a documented reason each is thrown, never caught and silently discarded.
- An overdue report using an injected `Clock`, tested at the exact due-date boundary and one day past it.
- A trace showing a rejected checkout leaves the catalog's available-copy count unchanged.

## Review and completion
A reviewer adds a new loan rule (a hold/reservation queue for a book with zero available copies) and asks you to identify every class that must change versus every class that must not. The catalog's invariants must survive concurrent-looking sequences of checkout/return calls issued in an unexpected order. This project uses only the standard library; no database or framework is required or expected.
learningObjectives: Model a domain with records, a sealed result type, and a custom checked/unchecked exception hierarchy
Protect a collection-backed invariant (copies available) against every operation that could violate it
Choose collections by actual access pattern (lookup by ISBN, ordered overdue listing)
Write boundary-driven tests for the last-copy and no-copies edge cases before implementing them
Keep a clock injectable so date-dependent behavior remains deterministic and testable
